targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "${measurement}" and r._field == "count")
  |> sum()
  |> keep(columns: ["_value"])

from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "${measurement}")
  |> keep(columns: ["address"])
  |> group()
  |> distinct(column: "address")
  |> count()

panels.title: Telegrams of unknown devices
panels.description: Addresses which are not configured in the integration. A device you just pressed a button on shows up here.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "${measurement}" and r._field == "count" and r.known == "False")
  |> sum()
  |> keep(columns: ["_value"])

from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "${measurement}")
  |> keep(columns: ["gateway_id"])
  |> group()
  |> distinct(column: "gateway_id")
  |> count()

from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "${measurement}" and r._field == "count")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: sum, createEmpty: false)
  |> group(columns: ["direction", "_time"])
  |> sum()
  |> group(columns: ["direction"])
  |> rename(columns: {_value: "telegrams"})

panels.title: Telegram rate by gateway
panels.description: With several gateways on one radio/bus the same telegram is received more than once - that is expected.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "${measurement}" and r._field == "count")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: sum, createEmpty: false)
  |> group(columns: ["gateway_id", "_time"])
  |> sum()
  |> group(columns: ["gateway_id"])

from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "${measurement}" and r._field == "count")
  |> group(columns: ["address", "device_name"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 20)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ label: if exists r.device_name and r.device_name != "" then r.device_name else r.address, telegrams: r._value }))

from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "${measurement}" and r._field == "count")
  |> group(columns: ["msg_type"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)

panels.title: Telegrams per EEP

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "${measurement}" and r._field == "count")
  |> group(columns: ["eep"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with eep: if r.eep == "" then "not configured" else r.eep }))
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)

panels.description: Telegrams of addresses which are not configured have no EEP - they are summarized as 'not configured' instead of a nameless slice.

panels.title: Unknown devices (not configured yet)
panels.description: Sorted by the number of telegrams. Use 'Devices -> + add device' in the Eltako web ui to configure them.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "${measurement}" and r._field == "count" and r.known == "False")
  |> group(columns: ["address", "msg_type", "gateway_id"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 50)
  |> keep(columns: ["address", "msg_type", "gateway_id", "_value"])
  |> rename(columns: {_value: "telegrams"})

panels.title: Configured vs. unconfigured addresses over time
panels.description: Telegrams of addresses which are not part of the configuration. Press a button on a device and its telegrams appear here - the fastest way to find out which address it uses.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "${measurement}" and r._field == "count")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: sum, createEmpty: false)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with state: if r.known == "True" then "configured" else "not configured" }))
  |> group(columns: ["state", "_time"])
  |> sum()
  |> group(columns: ["state"])

panels.title: Most active unconfigured addresses (with their last payload)
panels.description: Click an address to open the 'Product and test inspector' with all of its telegrams.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "${measurement}" and r._field == "data" and r.known == "False")
  |> group(columns: ["address", "msg_type"])
  |> reduce(identity: {telegrams: 0, payload: ""},
            fn: (r, accumulator) => ({ telegrams: accumulator.telegrams + 1, payload: r._value }))
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["telegrams"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 20)
  |> keep(columns: ["address", "msg_type", "telegrams", "payload"])
